question: Sixteen hours after delivery, a newborn develops respiratory distress. She was born at 38 weeks' gestation with a birth weight of 3200 g (7 lb 1 oz). Pregnancy was complicated by polyhydramnios. Physical examination shows tachypnea and bluish discoloration of the extremities. Auscultation of the chest shows diffuse crackles in the lung fields and a harsh holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. Abdominal x-ray shows absence of bowel gas. Which of the following best explains the pathogenesis of this newborn's condition?

options.opb: Deletion in the long arm of chromosome 7
options.ope: Deletion in the long arm of chromosome 22

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Defect in the pleuroperitoneal membrane" -> "Diaphragmatic hernia" -> "Abdominal organs in thoracic cavity" -> "Impaired lung development" -> "Respiratory distress" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Deletion in the long arm of chromosome 7" -> "Cystic fibrosis" -> "Thick mucus in lungs" -> "Respiratory distress" -> "Possible" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Defect in mesodermal differentiation" -> "Congenital heart defect" -> "Holosystolic murmur" -> "Heart failure" -> "Respiratory distress" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Absence of dynein" -> "Ciliary dyskinesia" -> "Impaired mucociliary clearance" -> "Respiratory distress" -> "Possible" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Deletion in the long arm of chromosome 22" -> "DiGeorge syndrome" -> "Cardiac defect" -> "Holosystolic murmur" -> "Heart failure" -> "Respiratory distress" -> 80%
analysis: The newborn's symptoms, including respiratory distress, polyhydramnios, and the presence of a harsh holosystolic murmur, suggest a congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), which is often due to a defect in the pleuroperitoneal membrane. The absence of bowel gas on the abdominal x-ray supports this diagnosis, as the intestines may be herniated into the thoracic cavity, affecting lung development and function.
